method: Enumerate every raw/*/source_pages.json record, compare exact URLs with iteration362 census, verify the fifteen outside pages against immutable iteration165 cache evidence, retain exact DOM tables and prose for subsequent coverage comparison. Existing extraction is not declared absent merely because its page is outside the supplemental census.
limitations: Only source_pages.json inventory is reconciled; other record kinds and uncached URLs remain outside this audit.
Unreviewed table and prose evidence is not extracted game mechanics.
Network suspension preserved; canonical IDs, historical applicability and operative values remain unresolved.

prose_blocks.html: Focuses on improved melee damage. Taken from Tar'iia Tem'erae in Hathor Zhi, The Dark Academy — /loc -74004, 18235, -10687. The chain runs through Donovan at Donovan's Roost, who sets the Blade of Oppression quest. Grants Avatar of Ghalnn, Blood Hammer I-V, Hammer of Carnage I-IV, Speed of Ghalnn and Truncheon of Ghalnn I-III. Grants the title Warcaller. The choice is not permanent. prose_blocks.html: Focuses on improved support. Taken in Tanvu — the guide names Horichi Ji at /loc 45700, -20795, 4565, while a player's account names Hana Pho, the Cleric instructor there. Of the two names recorded for its trainer, Hana Pho is the one the archive can corroborate: she is among the four Cleric instructors who offer Affinity Removal.

prose_blocks.html: Ferocity and mystical power. Dragon practitioners meet force with overwhelming force and do not yield. Their attacks hit hard and cost much, and they learn the mystical side of the dragon too — to leap like the cloud dragon, gleam like the sun dragon, and become resilient like the stone dragon.

prose_blocks.html:
36 of this class's abilities belong to this style — a Monk on another path never learns them.

How it is chosen Chosen at Choose Your Path (922), which sends you to Kiyo at the Imperial Training Center near the Magi Hold in Kojan. Three quests follow, ending at A Force Of Will (2702). This branch can be completed on the VGO Emulator. A Monk chooses a martial style at level 15. The choice is not permanent: A Step Backward (2838) sends a Monk back to Brithrax Lightstorm with a letter both other masters must sign, after which a different style may be taken.

prose_blocks.html: Deception and unseen power. Drunken practitioners keep themselves off balance, striking from impossible angles and tempting opponents into openings that do not exist. They stagger to dodge and to infuriate, and counterattack from that evasiveness. The style leans more on defence and on managing hatred than the dragon does.

prose_blocks.html: Redirection and debilitation. The harmonious monk deflects an attacker's own force to their disadvantage, using minimal strength and leading the attacker off balance in one seamless movement. It leans on a clear mind and the power of the spirit, and most of its abilities leave the enemy weakened in a way that can then be exploited.

record.notes: Archive class-page observation only. Base versus race-adjusted meaning, live-era applicability and primary provenance are not established. Page game id is not adopted as a canonical client ID. No stance or learned-ability claims extracted.

record.name: Offensive Style

style_observation.effect_text: Allows you to study your opponent and enter the base Offensive Style, setting you up to gain melee damage, while lowering your parry and dodge. Effects increase the longer you fight an opponent.
style_observation.attribution_text: Read from the VGO Emulator client. No source this archive draws on recorded the Ranger's styles.

record.source_card_html:
Offensive Style · from level 1 Allows you to study your opponent and enter the base Offensive Style, setting you up to gain melee damage, while lowering your parry and dodge. Effects increase the longer you fight an opponent.
Where this comes from Read from the VGO Emulator client. No source this archive draws on recorded the Ranger's styles.

record.name: Evasive Style

style_observation.effect_text: Allows you to study your opponent and enter the base Evasive Style, setting you up to gain parry and dodge while still focusing on melee combat. Effects increase the longer you fight an opponent.
style_observation.attribution_text: Read from the VGO Emulator client. No source this archive draws on recorded the Ranger's styles.

record.source_card_html:
Evasive Style · from level 1 Allows you to study your opponent and enter the base Evasive Style, setting you up to gain parry and dodge while still focusing on melee combat. Effects increase the longer you fight an opponent.
Where this comes from Read from the VGO Emulator client. No source this archive draws on recorded the Ranger's styles.

record.name: Style of Precision

style_observation.effect_text: Allows you to study your opponent and enter the base Precision Style, setting you up to gain ranged damage and range, while lowering your damage, parry, and dodge. Effects increase the longer you fight an opponent.
style_observation.attribution_text: Read from the VGO Emulator client. No source this archive draws on recorded the Ranger's styles.

prose_blocks.html: These are recorded here from the fan wikis, but nobody has yet opened the VGO Emulator client and confirmed them. They may be exactly right, they may carry figures the game never used, or they may not be in the emulator at all — there is no way to tell from the sources alone. Of this class's 203 abilities, 109 have had their tooltip read in game, 53 more were seen in the client's spellbook, and 24 were looked for and not found. Where a tooltip has been read it overrides the wikis, and around four in five disagreed with them — so treat the figures below with care.
